subject: Private Deploy: Sovereign circuit & HA modes — localization, DR window, and vendor peering
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@nordbank.com>

Cc: NordBank SRE <sre@nordbank.com>

Subject: Inquiry: Sovereign private deploy & HA peering — NordBank

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this early look. We’re preparing a procurement packet for a private deployment of Redwood into our regional VPCs and have a few hard constraints and technical questions up front so we can size the SOW and acceptance criteria:

1) Data residency: EU primary (Frankfurt) with an APAC warm-standby (Tokyo/Singapore). Latency-sensitive requests stay in-region. We need a clear diagram and the guarantees around no cross-border payload egress except for control-plane telemetry that’s explicitly approved.

2) Failover mode: warm-standby with automated promotion. What is your recommended degradation window (expected RTO/RPO), and can we limit automatic promotion to manual ops approval?

3) KMS/HSM: Keys must be EU-resident for primary data. Can your private deployment integrate with our HSM (Thales) via dedicated peering and meet FIPS requirements?

4) Network peering & routing: we use private interconnect (Cloud Interconnect) and require BGP community tagging to enforce egress controls. Any constraints on BGP communities, ASN mapping, or MTU during cutover?

5) Acceptance tests and evidence: we’ll need runbooks and sample telemetry (audit logs, TLS cert fingerprints, control-plane auth logger) to satisfy our audit team.

Attached: high-level residency_requirements doc.

Can you send a short architecture sketch and proposed cutover cadence by EOD Thursday? Also include the expected procurement lead time for Dedicated + Warm Standby pricing.

Regards,
Oliver
Director, Cloud Security — NordBank

Attachment: nordbank_residency_requirements.pdf

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can meet strict EU residency for primary, deliver an APAC warm-standby, and integrate with an on-prem HSM via private peering. I’ll summarize options below and propose next steps.

High-level options (tradeoffs):
- Option A — EU-primary + APAC warm-standby (recommended): EU handles production traffic. APAC sits in warm-standby with KV cache pre-warm and automatic promotion guarded by manual ops approval. Lower cross-border egress; slower failover (~10–20m) but minimal replication overhead.
- Option B — Active-active with geo-routing: lower failover time but requires strict tenant pinning and full data replication (higher cost, more complex controls).

KMS/HSM: We support HSM proxying over private circuits. For Thales we’ll run a compatibility checklist (KMIP over private peering + mutual TLS). We’ll want a dedicated control tunnel to avoid any mixed-control-plane telemetry crossing borders.

Network/cutover constraints: BGP and ASN mapping are supported; we ask customers to reserve an advertised ASN range and provide BGP communities for egress tagging. MTU mismatch during cutover is a known friction point — we recommend 1500 end-to-end or explicit path MTU prechecks.

Acceptance tests & runbooks: attached is a short options notes PDF with what we’ll supply (topology sketch, cutover steps, preflight tests, and sample audit artifacts).

Next steps:
1) Tech sync (30–45m) with your network/SRE and our infra team (Karthik and Soojin) — propose Thu 2026-05-07 09:00 CET / 00:00 PT.
2) We’ll send a draft SOW + acceptance checklist within 48 hours after sync.
3) If you can share preferred maintenance windows and procurement timeline that helps finalize pricing.

I’ll let Karthik follow up with the concrete cutover sequence and KMS notes.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 5, 2026 at 12:02 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’ll let Karthik follow up with the concrete cutover sequence and KMS notes.

Oliver / team — quick technical appendix and an initial cutover/checklist for the warm-standby pattern (EU primary, APAC warm):

Recommended topology (short):
- Control plane: single-authority in EU (Frankfurt) with a read-only control-plane replica in APAC. API tokens are scoped regionally; token issuance and rotation remain EU-originated.
- Data plane: tenant data stored in EU. Warm-standby keeps checkpointed model shards and KV caches; synchronous metadata replication only for critical state, async bulk replication for large data.
- KMS: integrate via dedicated private peering; we support a proxy mode where customer-hosted HSM responds to decryption calls via mutually authenticated TLS. This avoids copying keys to APAC.

Cutover sequence (condensed):
T-60m: run preflight (BGP session validation, MTU checks, certificate sanity, KMS connectivity).
T-15m: pause background bulk replication and drain long-running requests.
T-5m: freeze new writes to EU tenant layer; validate KV checkpoint in APAC.
T+0: flip routing by toggling BGP communities and promoting APAC read-only to accept writes (manual confirmation required per policy).
T+5–20m: smoke tests (token exchange, KMS decrypt, end-to-end inference on canary tenant).
T+30m: resume bulk replication and post-cutover monitoring for 72h.

Acceptance checklist (examples):
- KMS decrypt success rate >= 99% on canary traffic.
- No cross-border payload egress in production paths (control plane metadata allowed after approved list).
- Audit logs (auth, token rotation, operator actions) exported to customer logging endpoint within 5m.
- Failback test executed within 24h in dry-run mode.

Notes about BGP/peering: we can honor BGP community tags and will advertise customer-preferred egress through your interconnect. We do ask for a /29 for peering and a planned ASN to ensure no overlap.

I attached the minimal network circuit requirement text and a short playbook for KMS sync. Happy to walk through the checklist on the call.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
